answer: Rotating marble assignment: each epoch, a verifiable random function derives a public seed no one can predict before the epoch closes. Every identity must then claim, within a fixed window, a position on a shared terrace of slots whose ordering is fixed by that seed, and posting a valid signal requires occupying a slot proven consistent with the seed. Because attackers cannot precompute which slots stay cheap or which collide, mass registration forces them to buy slots across every possible ordering, paying the full slot price plus failed-claim fees per identity each epoch.
